chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ, from Aḥmad ibn ʿĀʾidh, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, who said:
One day Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام began with us and said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:
Whoever dies while there is no Imam over him, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah.
So I said: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم say that? He said: Yes, by Allah, he indeed said it.
I said: So everyone who dies while there is no Imam for him, then his death is a death of Jāhiliyyah? He said: Yes.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the speaker narrating the prophetic statement
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely appointed leader whose authority is binding
key_terms.جَاهِلِيَّةٍ: the pre-Islamic condition of ignorance, misguidance, and lack of rightful authority
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, from whom this statement is transmitted
key_terms.مِيتَةُ جَاهِلِيَّةٍ: a death resembling the state of pre-Islamic ignorance and estrangement from true guidance

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith 'whoever dies without an Imam dies the death of Jāhiliyyah' mean?
ai.summary: This hadith states that dying without an Imam is described as dying a death of Jāhiliyyah. It emphasizes the necessity of having and recognizing divinely ordained religious authority. In Shia doctrine, it is a foundational text concerning Imamate and the obligation of allegiance to the Imam of guidance.
